\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\cat}[1]{\mathcal{#1}}
\begin{document}
\section{A short paper}
We consider a functor $F\colon \cat{C}\to \cat{D}$ and note that $n!$ grows.
\begin{theorem}[Main]
For every $x\ge 2$ the map $\phi_x$ is invertible.\footnote{See the appendix.}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Indeed $\phi_x$ is the composite $g\circ f$, where $f$ is given above.
\end{proof}
The class of such functors is denoted $\operatorname{Fun}(\cat{C},\cat{D})$.
